messages.subject: Re: fieldMask applied to thermal images
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

You also can trick the function by using the same layer number for all parameters and using only 1 layer on "myIndex". Please, check the example below:

EX1.RemSoil <- fieldMask(mosaic = EX1.Rotated, Red = 1, Green = 1, Blue = 1, myIndex = "Red",cropValue = 0.7, cropAbove = T)

Attention: You need to change the "cropValue" according to your thermal image pixel values.

Hope it helps...!

Best,
Filipe

messages.subject_clean: FIELDimageR: Re: fieldMask applied to thermal images
messages.body_plain:
Thank you guys for the support,

I couldn't load the thermal image using the fieldMask function as suggested. However, I created a three-band image using the thermal band. Now it works. Code below:

# Load the image
EX1 <- stack("Image.tiff")

# Creating a three-band image. Note that all the bands will be the same (thermal).
EX2  <- stack(c( EX1, EX1, EX1))

# Removing the soil background
EX2.RemSoil <- fieldMask(mosaic = EX2, Red=1, Green=1, Blue=1, myIndex="Red", cropValue = 4500, cropAbove = T)

Thanks,
Marcelo

messages.subject: Sampling areas within plots
messages.body_plain:
Hello Everyone!

We just started using FieldImageR and webODM , I was wondering if there is a way to create sampling areas within plots, so that you can have it only measure whats in the center of the plot to keep edge effects out? (We are using it in a weed science program so edge effects can show up in every plot with variability in spraying.)

thanks!
